info.title: Hologram Model Hub
info.summary: One endpoint for open models: find one, fetch it from a source that is up, and prove the bytes.
info.description:

`HF_ENDPOINT=https://gethologram.ai` for anything built on `huggingface_hub…

servers.description: Production. The hub is one host; there is no staging surface.

tags.name: Discovery

tags.description: Find a model and read its files, in Hugging Face's shape. This is the dialect every Python client already speaks.

publisherToken.description: A publisher token. Required to list, search or publish objects. Reads of a known address need no token.

privyToken.description: A Privy access token for the person signed in to the site, verified here against the app's ES256 public key. It is only ever accepted on `/api/account/*`; no read surface takes it, and it is stripped from every other route at the edge.

Descriptor.description: What the hub is and where everything under it lives. One fetch, no schema needed to read it.

catalog.description: Today's catalog object: the whole index in one address.

snapshot.description: The day this catalog was built.

fetch.description: The template for fetching any object by address.

kinds.description: The object kinds the hub publishes and what each holds.

AgentCard.description: The hub as a set of skills, for frameworks that discover a service through an agent card.

HologramFacts.description: What Hugging Face's row has no field for: where this model sits in the hub's index.

manifest.description: The index object for this model at this revision.

files.description: How many files the revision has.

parameters.description: Parameter count, when it is known.

listed.description: Absent or true on a model the current browse list carries, which is a row with the full facts. `false` on a model the browse list has forgotten: the hub still holds its bytes and serves every dialect for it, but the task, parameter count and download figures were never published with the object, so they are absent rather than zero.

context.description: Context length, when it is known.

sources.description: Which sources hold these bytes today, in display spelling. Three vocabularies describe the same sources and nothing else maps between them, so map here: `Hugging Face` is `huggingface.co` in `/api/hub/health` and `X-Hub-Source`, and `huggingface` in a `/via/` prefix; `ModelScope` is `modelscope.cn` and `modelscope`; `IPFS` is `ipfs` in both. `P2P` is a fourth source that appears on a few rows and …

ModelRow.description: One search result, in Hugging Face's list shape plus a `hologram` block.

ModelInfo.description: One model at the indexed revision, in Hugging Face's model-info shape.

sha.description: The indexed revision, always a full commit hash.

siblings.description: Every file of the revision, by name only.

TreeEntry.description: One file, with the hash a download must match.

type.description: Only files: the index holds no directory entries.

oid.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes, 64 hex characters, and the value a download must be checked against. **This differs from Hugging Face**, whose `oid` is a 40-character git blob SHA-1 and which carries the SHA-256 only inside `lfs`, only on large files. Here every file reports its SHA-256 in this field; the length is the tell. A client written against Hugging Face's meaning will read a perfectly go…

lfs.description: Present on large files, for clients that branch on it. Its `oid` repeats the SHA-256 above rather than differing from it.

oid.description: The SHA-256 of a file's bytes.

Refs.description: The branches the hub knows: exactly one.

HubHealth.description: Which byte sources are up, and the order the hub prefers them in.

ok.description: Whether the hub reached it on its last probe.

reason.description: Why the hub believes it, in one word. `verified` means the hub fetched bytes and they hashed correctly — from the hub's network.

order.description: Preference order. A file goes to the first source here that is `ok` and holds it.

Archive.description: Every day the hub has indexed, chained backwards, and the three places any day can be read from.

gateway.description: The IPFS gateway a day can be read through.

mirror.description: The hub own copy of the archive.

registry.description: The OCI repository that holds every day index.

catalog.description: That day's catalog object: the browse rows and the map from model id to address.

cid.description: The IPFS CID the day was pinned under.

source.description: The commit of the code that built it.

Pins.description: The models whose weights survive both Hugging Face and ModelScope being unreachable.

gateway.description: The IPFS gateway the hub redirects through.

root.description: The IPFS root CID of the model directory.

AccountHealth.description: Whether this hub offers sign-in at all.

configured.description: False when the hub has no sign-in keys. Every anonymous surface works either way.

Account.description: Everything the hub holds about one signed-in person, which is deliberately almost nothing.

did.description: The Privy decentralised identifier the token was issued for.

wallet.description: An address the person chose to report. Recorded, never trusted.

requests.description: How many models this account has asked for.

AccountError.description: How the account service refuses: one sentence, no code, because this surface has no clients but the site.

HubError.description: How every dialect route refuses: one sentence that names the fix, with a machine code in `X-Error-Code`.

OciError.description: How the registry dialect refuses, in the shape the OCI distribution spec requires.

OciManifest.description: An OCI image manifest. Every layer is one file of the model and its digest is that file's SHA-256, which is what makes a registry with no bytes of its own verifiable.

JsonRpcRequest.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request. `method` is an MCP method: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`.

JsonRpcResponse.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response. A failing tool answers `200` with `result.isError`, as MCP requires; only a malformed call gets `error`.

get.summary: The hub, answered three ways
get.description:
One URL, three readers, chosen by `Accept`.

A browser sends `text/html` and gets the website. A caller that asks for `application/json` by name gets the
